definitions.gloss: main topic, main subject, real issue
definitions.explanation: The central or primary topic of a conversation, meeting, or presentation. Often used when transitioning from preliminary remarks or small talk to the actual matter at hand.

examples.japanese: では、{本題|ほんだい}に{入|はい}りましょう。
examples.english: Well then, let's get to the main topic.

examples.japanese: {話|はなし}が{逸|そ}れたので、{本題|ほんだい}に{戻|もど}ります。
examples.english: The conversation got off track, so let me return to the main point.

examples.japanese: {前置|まえお}きが{長|なが}くなりましたが、{本題|ほんだい}に{入|はい}らせていただきます。
examples.english: I've been going on with the preamble, but allow me to move on to the main subject.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always appears in the fixed phrases {本題|ほんだい}に{入|はい}る (to get to the main topic) and {本題|ほんだい}に{戻|もど}る (to get back to the main topic). A very useful expression for meetings, presentations, and formal conversations. Often marks the transition from {前置|まえお}き (preamble) or {雑談|ざつだん} (small talk) to substantive discussion.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {本題|ほんだい}に{入|はい}る: to get to the main topic
- {本題|ほんだい}に{戻|もど}る: to return to the main topic
- {本題|ほんだい}から{逸|そ}れる: to stray from the main topic
